neighbours.label: naming a geological period (Cretaceous, Paleogene, Miocene), peaking near the name, as opposed to the same frames with a historical period, and to fossils and rocks with no period named
fire: The ammonites died out at the end of the Cretaceous.
These limestone beds date from the Late Jurassic of Portugal.
The fossil horse comes from the Miocene of Nebraska.
Coal formed in great swamps during the Carboniferous period.
The rocks span the boundary between Permian and Triassic.
Grasses spread widely through the Oligocene and Miocene.
The skull was found in Eocene sediments in Wyoming.
Sea levels rose sharply in the mid-Cretaceous.
quiet: The Vikings died out at the end of the Medieval period.
These limestone walls date from the Late Roman town of Merida.
The fossil horse comes from a gravel pit in Nebraska.
Wool was sold in great markets during the Georgian period.
The tombs span the boundary between Bronze and Iron Age.
Railways spread widely through the Victorian and Edwardian years.
The skull was found in sandstone sediments in Wyoming.
Sea levels rose sharply in the mid-Victorian years.

notes: Card: ' the' x6, ' ' x3, ' K' x3, ' (', '6', '–', around Cretaceous, Paleogene, Pliocene. Output promotes ' Pale', ' Cam', ' M'.
